prompt:
Create one full-body original 2D comic moth character on a transparent background, with every antenna tip, wing, hand, and foot fully inside the canvas. Use the original and v3 references for continuity. Keep the broad warm cream face, compact cream bean-shaped torso, confident charcoal outline, chartreuse wings and antenna tips, and chartreuse feet. Use restrained flat color and appealing drawn shapes. No scene, text, props, glow, texture, cast shadow, or extra character.

Preserve the established long antenna on the viewer's right in the front view and the shorter one opposite. They are flexible narrow stems ending in smooth rounded oblong paddles, about one-fifth less bulky than the references. No leaf vein, feather teeth, antenna fingers, or new ear shapes. Reduce the head's repeated cloud scallops to a small off-center crown tuft, one grouped cheek flare on each side, and a clean curved lower jaw. Keep a small irregular cream thorax ruff with two or three grouped soft tufts, not an even flower collar. Solid dark oval eyes, movable lids and separate brows, a small expressive mouth; no nose. For this anatomy master leave glasses off so the base face is visible. Make the expression attentive and warmly amused, with unequal brows and a restrained smile rather than a compulsory wide greeting.

Correct the wings decisively. Each side has a broad tapered forewing overlapping a smaller rounded hindwing, giving four discernible wing panels arranged as two natural paired appendages. The near pair shows a clear short overlap seam and a distinct forewing tip above a compact lower hindwing fan; the far pair follows the same construction in perspective. They hinge from the upper back and rest diagonally behind the torso, one pair slightly more open than the other. Preserve readable gaps around the elbows. The silhouette must show overlapping wings with different shapes, not two uninterrupted shoulder-to-floor sheets. No scalloped cape hem, cloth folds, neck clasp, long trailing tails, or identical repeated lobes. Add exactly one subdued darker-chartreuse oblong wing marking to each visible forewing; no concentric eyespot rings, pupil dots, or dense veins.

Use the v3 articulation: compact body weight, room for elbows and wrists, two arms in front of the wings, three grouped rounded fingers and a thumb, and short legs capable of a knee bend. Blunt rounded feet without cuffs or soles; avoid long pointed shoes. Pose the character in a relaxed three-quarter weight shift, one foot planted and the other resting lightly on its toe. Shoulder and hip angles gently oppose each other. One elbow bends with a modest open palm mid-explanation; the other hand rests naturally near the belly. The head turns toward us while the longer antenna subtly leans toward an interesting detail just outside frame. Keep the gesture relaxed enough to judge the anatomy. No rubber-hose skinny limbs, bodybuilding chest, costume, extra arms, or wings functioning as hands.
status: Superseded exploration. Wing structure improved; user rejected elongated adult proportions.
feedback: Restore the small innocent charm of earlier renders: larger soft head relative to body, compact torso, little hands, short feet. User-supplied earlier renders are references for this quality, not an approved final model.
